title: magnolia acuminata subsp. cordata
intro: Magnolia acuminata subsp. cordata, commonly known as the Narrow-leaved Sweetgum or Eastern Sweetgum, is a subspecies of the Magnolia acuminata tree, native to North America. The bark, leaves, and roots of this plant have been used in traditional medicine for their health benefits, which include anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antioxidant properties. The therapeutic actions of Magnolia acuminata subsp. cordata include analgesic, anti-diarrheal, and antipyretic effects, as well as the ability to treat respiratory and digestive issues. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and alkaloids, which are responsible for its medicinal properties.
